There's much more of it in dark chocolate than in milk chocolate.

hints: They grow under the ground.
You can also mash them.
They're brown on the outside and white inside.
questions.fun_fact: Belgium and France both say they invented French fries.

hints: It is a planned city, built almost from scratch.

It is in Nigeria.
questions.fun_fact: Nigeria moved its capital to Abuja partly because it is closer to the center of the country than Lagos.

These colors are known as “Pan-African” colors.
The same three colors appear on a traffic light.

It's the continent of safaris and “The Lion King”.

Without it, the fertile land would slowly turn into sand.

hints: Asia is much bigger than China.
Many countries fit inside Asia.
Africa, Europe and South America are one too.

questions.answer: At hydrothermal vents on the seafloor

Its bacteria use chemicals instead of light.

The male is so tiny that he stays stuck to the female for the rest of his life.
If the female were the size of a car, the male would be the size of a finger.

hints: It is much higher up than where airplanes fly.
It begins above the height where the International Space Station circles Earth.
Its name starts with a Greek prefix that means “outside.”

hints: It appears when something gets extremely hot.
It's a gas so hot that its atoms lose electrons.
It shares its name with a kind of old flat-screen TV.
questions.fun_fact: Lightning heats the air to about 30,000 °C (54,000 °F), roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.

questions.fun_fact: People called 1816 “the year without a summer”, and the bad weather kept Mary Shelley indoors, where she wrote “Frankenstein”.

It doesn't move at all in a quake

questions.question: King You lit the beacon fires just to make Bao Si laugh. Which era began soon after his fall?
hints: This era is known for great thinkers such as Confucius and Laozi.
It is often split into the Spring and Autumn and the Warring States periods.
After King You's fall, the court moved its capital east to Luoyi (洛邑).
questions.fun_fact: The story gave Chinese the idiom 烽火戏诸侯 (fēng huǒ xì zhū hóu, “playing tricks on the lords with beacon fires”), and the capital moved east in 770 BCE.

questions.description: Hunan's favourite home dish: so hot that the rice bowl calls for help.
questions.question: In the Hunan dish 辣椒炒肉 (làjiāo chǎo ròu, "stir-fried meat with chilli"), the name just says 肉. Which meat is it?
hints: In most Chinese dish names, 肉 on its own means the same everyday meat.
It's the meat in 红烧肉 (hóngshāo ròu) and in 回锅肉 (huíguō ròu) too.
This meat comes from the animal of the last year in the Chinese zodiac.
questions.fun_fact: Chillies only reached China from the Americas about 400 years ago, yet today Hunan is one of the spiciest places to eat in the world.

questions.description: The best part of this dinner is the part stuck to the bottom of the pot.
questions.question: Look at the photo: rice cooked in a clay pot, topped with sausage, with a crispy crust at the bottom. Which of the eight great cuisines is it from?
hints: It's a classic winter dish in the south of China and in Hong Kong.
The same cuisine is famous for dim sum and morning tea (早茶).
Its home province's capital is Guangzhou.
questions.fun_fact: The crispy rice crust at the bottom of the pot is called 饭焦 (fàn jiāo) in Cantonese, and many people scrape the pot to get every bit of it.

questions.description: Some say too much of a good thing is still a good thing. These farmers disagree.
questions.question: Long ago, ten of me rose in the sky together and the earth grew too hot. The archer Hou Yi shot down nine of us. What am I?
hints: Today there is only one of me left.
I give light and heat every day.
I rise in the east each morning.
questions.fun_fact: Hou Yi's wife is Chang'e (嫦娥), who in a famous legend flew to the moon, and China named its moon probes after her.

questions.description: Nature's crunchiest snack, with a panda on the other end.
questions.question: Pandas crunch bamboo stems all day long. Which of these is NOT true about bamboo stems?
hints: Think about where a bamboo stem comes from.
Three of these you could check by cutting or watching a bamboo stem.
Bamboo is actually a giant kind of grass.
questions.fun_fact: Bamboo is a giant grass, and some kinds can grow almost 1 m in a single day.

questions.description: Long before telescopes, a small child had a very creative guess about what was hanging in the night sky.
questions.question: Which Tang dynasty poet wrote 古朗月行 (gǔ lǎng yuè xíng), which starts “小时不识月，呼作白玉盘”?
hints: He loved wine and travelled all over China.
People call him the “Immortal of Poetry” (诗仙).
He also wrote 静夜思, the poem that starts “床前明月光”.
questions.fun_fact: In the poem, the child calls the moon a “white jade plate” (白玉盘) and wonders if it is a mirror flying above the clouds.

questions.description: Cash is feeling very lonely in its wallet these days.
questions.question: I was born in Japan in 1994 to keep track of car parts. Now I sit on almost every shop counter in China, and you scan me with your phone to pay. What am I?
hints: You need a phone camera to read me.
I'm a little square full of black and white dots.
Alipay and WeChat Pay show me on the screen too.
questions.fun_fact: The QR code was made by the Japanese company Denso Wave, and “QR” stands for “Quick Response”.

questions.description: The smallest coin in your piggy bank got a makeover, and a tough one.
questions.question: Today's 1-jiao (角) coin shows an orchid, is silver in color and stopped being made of aluminum in 2005. What is it made of now?
hints: The 2005 change made the coin harder-wearing and a bit heavier.
It's an alloy, a mix of metals, made mostly of iron.
It's the same metal as many kitchen sinks and spoons.
questions.fun_fact: It takes 10 jiao to make 1 yuan, so ten of these little orchid coins buy the same as one big 1-yuan coin.

questions.description: This torch travelled further than most families go on their summer holidays.
questions.question: This traditional good-luck design swirls over the red-and-silver Beijing 2008 Olympic torch, which was even named after it. What is it?
hints: It is often painted on old palace ceilings and embroidered on festive clothes.
It has nothing to do with animals or plants.
Look up at the sky on a sunny day and you may see the real thing.
questions.fun_fact: The Beijing 2008 torch was designed by a team from the Chinese computer company Lenovo.

questions.description: Handle with care: this question breaks if you drop it.
questions.question: Jingdezhen, China's “Porcelain Capital” (瓷都), is most famous for ware like this. What is this style called?
hints: Its patterns are painted on before the glaze goes on, then fired.
The colour comes from cobalt, and it reached its height in the Yuan and Ming dynasties.
Jay Chou has a famous song with this porcelain's name as its title.
questions.fun_fact: Jingdezhen got its name from the Song emperor Zhenzong, whose reign name Jingde (景德) was stamped on the town's porcelain made for the palace.

questions.description: A love song that gets very poetic about one girl's cheeks.
questions.question: Complete the line from the Xinjiang folk song “Lift Your Veil” (掀起你的盖头来): “Your face is red and round, like ___ in autumn.”
hints: Like the other lines of the song, it compares the girl to something from nature.
It is something people pick from a tree.
Xinjiang's Aksu region is famous for growing sweet ones of this fruit.
questions.fun_fact: Wang Luobin, called the “King of Western Folk Songs”, arranged this Uyghur song and made it famous all over China.

questions.description: A kitchen story so famous that philosophers still sharpen their minds on it.
questions.question: The idiom 庖丁解牛 (páo dīng jiě niú, “Cook Ding carves an ox”) comes from a story in which ancient thinker's book?
hints: He lived during the Warring States period.
His book is full of playful fables, like a giant fish that turns into a huge bird.
He once dreamed he was a butterfly and woke up unsure which one he really was.
questions.fun_fact: In Zhuangzi’s story, the cook used the same knife for 19 years and it was still as sharp as new.

questions.description: Seven thousand years before house-hunting apps, someone still had to choose a good home.
questions.question: About 7,000 years ago at Hemudu (河姆渡), people lived on wet ground and grew rice. What kind of houses did they build?
hints: Hemudu is in the warm, rainy south, near today's Ningbo in Zhejiang.
The builders had to deal with floods, damp ground, snakes and wild animals.
The living space sat up in the air, with the ground left open below.
questions.fun_fact: Hemudu builders already joined wooden beams with mortise and tenon joints (榫卯), which hold together without nails.

questions.description: Yaks live up here, and nobody has ever had to clean the gutters.
questions.question: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (青藏高原) is called the “Roof of the World” (世界屋脊). What is its average height above sea level?
hints: No other large plateau on Earth is as high.
Many visitors get altitude sickness there, even when they stand still.
Lhasa, at about 3,650 m, actually sits lower than the plateau's average.
questions.fun_fact: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau is still rising by a few millimetres a year, because the Indian plate keeps pushing into Asia.

questions.description: A province where winter is long and some street signs speak two languages.
questions.question: Their families crossed the Tumen River over 150 years ago, and Jilin is home to more of them than any other province. Which ethnic group is it?
hints: Their traditional dances often feature long, hourglass-shaped drums.
Their language is also spoken just across the border.
They are famous for cold noodles and spicy pickled cabbage.
questions.fun_fact: Street signs in Yanji, the capital of Jilin's Yanbian prefecture, are written in both Chinese and Korean.

questions.description: A goodbye poem where the only one waving might be the river.
questions.question: I grew up in Shu (蜀), today's Sichuan. As a young man I sailed down the Yangtze past Jingmen and wrote “Farewell at Jingmen Ferry” (渡荆门送别). Who am I?
hints: I lived in the Tang dynasty and spent much of my life travelling.
After leaving Sichuan, I never went back to live there.
I loved wine and the moon, and people call me the “Immortal of Poetry” (诗仙).
questions.fun_fact: The Qing critic Shen Deqian said the poem shows no farewell at all, so the word “farewell” could be cut from its title.

questions.description: Sand that refuses to blow away and water where no water should be: nature clearly ignored the rules here.
questions.question: This desert in Inner Mongolia joined the World Heritage list in 2024. It has the world's tallest stationary sand dunes and over 100 lakes. Which desert is it?
questions.answer: Badain Jaran Desert (巴丹吉林沙漠)
hints: It lies in western Inner Mongolia, in Alxa League (阿拉善盟).
Its UNESCO listing calls it a place of “towers of sand and lakes”.
It is the northwestern neighbour of the Tengger Desert.
questions.fun_fact: Some of Badain Jaran's dunes rise about 500 m (1,640 ft) above their base, and the lakes between them are fed by groundwater whose source scientists still debate.

questions.description: Yangzhou's lake went on a diet and kept its famous sister's name.
questions.question: You're on a boat on Slender West Lake (瘦西湖) in Yangzhou. Which sight will you NOT see there?
hints: Three of these sights are in Yangzhou; one belongs to another famous lake.
The odd one out appears in the Legend of the White Snake.
It stands beside the “fat” West Lake in Hangzhou.
questions.fun_fact: Du Mu's Tang poem line “二十四桥明月夜” (Twenty-Four Bridges on a moonlit night) made Yangzhou's bridges famous long before today's scenic area was built.

questions.description: The one day of the year when banging on the door at dawn is a welcome, and quite possibly a profitable, thing to do.
questions.question: At dawn, firecrackers go off, shops reopen, and families welcome the God of Wealth (财神). Which day of the New Year is it?
hints: It falls inside the first week of the New Year.
Many shops stay closed until this day and then open their doors again.
On this day many New Year taboos end, like the ban on sweeping the floor, and many families eat dumplings that morning.
questions.fun_fact: Some shop owners try to set off the very first firecracker on this morning, hoping the God of Wealth visits their shop before any other.

questions.description: Twelve animals lined up for a race, and the prize was a job on the calendar for ever.
questions.question: I can fly and bring rain. In the Great Race I came after the Rabbit and before the Snake. Nobody has ever seen me in real life. Who am I?
hints: I am the fifth animal of the Chinese zodiac.
At New Year, dancers hold me up on long poles and make me wave through the streets.
Chinese people sometimes call themselves my descendants (龙的传人).
questions.fun_fact: In many tellings of the Great Race, the Dragon could have won but stopped to bring rain to a village, or to help the Rabbit across the river.

questions.description: A porridge with so many beans, nuts and dates in it that it could pass for a whole grocery shop in a bowl.
questions.question: Laba congee is cooked with grains, beans, nuts and dates on the 8th day of the 12th lunar month. Eating it starts the countdown to which festival?
hints: The 12th lunar month is the last month of the year.
An old saying goes 过了腊八就是年 (guò le Làbā jiù shì nián).
It is the festival with red packets, couplets and the reunion dinner.
questions.fun_fact: Many Buddhist temples in China give out free Laba congee on this day, and people queue in the cold winter morning for a bowl.

questions.description: Four lines, no more, no less: the Tang dynasty's version of a tweet.
questions.question: I wrote seven-character jueju (七言绝句) so well that people called me their “Sage Hand” (七绝圣手). I wrote “Out to the Frontier” (出塞). Who am I?
hints: I lived in the Tang dynasty, at the same time as Li Bai.
Many of my famous poems are about soldiers at the frontier and about saying goodbye to friends.
I also wrote “Seeing Xin Jian Off at Lotus Tower” (芙蓉楼送辛渐), and I share my family name with Wang Wei.
questions.fun_fact: A legend says Wang Changling, Gao Shi and Wang Zhihuan once sat in a tavern and secretly counted which of their poems the singers performed most.

questions.description: Good news travelled slowly in the Tang dynasty, but it still made a poet dance.
questions.question: Du Fu wrote the joyful poem “Hearing the Army Has Recovered Henan and Hebei” (闻官军收河南河北) when the An Lushan Rebellion ended. In which century?
hints: The Tang dynasty lasted from 618 to 907.
Du Fu was a younger friend of Li Bai and wrote in the middle part of the Tang dynasty.
The rebellion broke out in 755 and ended a few years later.
questions.fun_fact: The Qing scholar Pu Qilong called it Du Fu's “first happy poem of his life” (生平第一快诗).

questions.description: Monks, sword fighters and a few hundred stairs too many: welcome to Hubei's holy heights.
questions.question: These halls stand on Mount Wudang (武当山) in Hubei, a mountain famous for its own style of kung fu. Which religion built them?
hints: Its temples and priests can be found on many famous mountains across China.
Its old teacher Laozi (老子) wrote the Dao De Jing (道德经).
Its symbol is the black-and-white yin-yang circle (太极图).
questions.fun_fact: The Golden Hall on Wudang's highest peak was cast from bronze and covered in gold in 1416, during the Ming dynasty.
